easy.question: To which land did Jacob and the children of Israel come?
answers: Egypt
Canaan
Midian
easy.explanation: Verse 1 says that the children of Israel came into Egypt.

easy.question: How many people came from Jacob’s descendants?
answers: Twelve
Seventy
Two hundred
easy.explanation: Verse 5 states that the number of people was seventy.

easy.question: Which of the following appears in the list of the children of Israel?
answers: Moses
Aaron
Asher
easy.explanation: Asher appears in the list of the children of Israel in verse 4.

medium.question: What is the order of events described in these verses?
answers: Jacob and his sons come to Egypt, Joseph and that generation die, and the children of Israel multiply
The children of Israel multiply, Jacob comes to Egypt, and Joseph dies
Joseph dies, Jacob goes down to Egypt, and then the sons are listed
medium.explanation: First the descent into Egypt is described, then Joseph and that generation die, and finally the children of Israel multiply.

medium.question: What does the phrase “came out of the loins of Jacob” mean in this context?
answers: People who traveled with Jacob
Jacob’s descendants
People who were born in Egypt
medium.explanation: The phrase “came out of the loins of Jacob” refers to his descendants; the context shows that these were the seventy people counted.

medium.question: What happened after Joseph, his brothers, and that entire generation died?
answers: The children of Israel returned to Canaan
The number of the children of Israel remained unchanged
The children of Israel multiplied greatly, and the land was filled with them
medium.explanation: Verse 7 says that the children of Israel were fruitful, multiplied, became very mighty, and filled the land.

challenge.question: Which detail in verse 5 shows that Joseph was already in Egypt before the rest of the family arrived?
answers: It explicitly says, “Joseph was in Egypt already”
It says that Joseph was the firstborn
It says that Joseph came out of Jacob’s loins
challenge.explanation: The verse separately states that Joseph was already in Egypt, while the other family members are described as coming there.

challenge.question: What does the accumulation of the verbs “were fruitful, and increased abundantly, and multiplied, and waxed exceeding mighty” emphasize?
answers: That the children of Israel moved from place to place
That their growth was great, rapid, and powerful
That they were mainly engaged in farming
challenge.explanation: The series of verbs emphasizes increasing growth: the children of Israel multiplied greatly and became numerous and strong.

challenge.question: What can be understood from the phrase “every man and his household came”?
answers: Only Jacob entered Egypt
Each Israelite came alone
Each man came with his household and family
challenge.explanation: The words “his household” expand the description beyond the individual man to include his family.

questions.question: Which detail in verse 5 shows that Joseph was already in Egypt before the rest of the family arrived?
answers: It explicitly says, “Joseph was in Egypt already”
It says that Joseph was the firstborn
It says that Joseph came out of Jacob’s loins
questions.explanation: The verse separately states that Joseph was already in Egypt, while the other family members are described as coming there.

answers: That the children of Israel moved from place to place

answers: Only Jacob entered Egypt

Each man came with his household and family
questions.explanation: The words “his household” expand the description beyond the individual man to include his family.

paragraphs.title: Pharaoh Becomes Afraid and Increases the Burden

easy.question: Who arose as king over Egypt?
answers: A new king
Joseph
The former Pharaoh
easy.explanation: Verse 8 says, “There arose up a new king over Egypt.”

easy.question: How did the king describe the people of Israel?
answers: Few and weak
Numerous and mighty
Rich and scattered
easy.explanation: The king said, “The people of the children of Israel are more and mightier than we.”

easy.question: What did the children of Israel build for Pharaoh?
answers: Palaces in Jerusalem
Temples in the wilderness
Treasure cities
easy.explanation: Verse 11 says that they built Pithom and Raamses, which were treasure cities, for Pharaoh.

medium.question: Why was the king of Egypt afraid of the children of Israel?
answers: He feared they would multiply and help Egypt’s enemies in war
He feared they would not work in the fields
He feared they would leave Egypt immediately
medium.explanation: The king feared that if war broke out, the children of Israel would join Egypt’s enemies and fight against Egypt.

medium.question: What does the phrase “let us deal wisely with them” mean in context?
answers: Let us flee from them
Let us act against them by using a scheme
Let us teach them wisdom
medium.explanation: The context shows that the king proposed finding a clever strategy to harm the children of Israel and prevent them from multiplying.

medium.question: What was the result of the affliction and hard labor imposed on the children of Israel?
answers: They disappeared from Egypt
They stopped working
They multiplied and grew even more
medium.explanation: The verse says, “The more they afflicted them, the more they multiplied and grew”; the affliction did not stop their growth.

challenge.question: What change in the treatment of the children of Israel is described between Joseph’s time and the time of the new king?
answers: The king who knew Joseph was replaced by one who did not know him
Joseph became king instead of Pharaoh
The children of Israel moved from Egypt to another land
challenge.explanation: The text emphasizes that the new king “knew not Joseph,” so he did not regard the Israelites with the recognition and appreciation shown earlier.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the fact that the children of Israel continued to multiply despite the affliction?
answers: The affliction was too mild
Their strength and endurance were greater than expected
The Egyptians stopped being afraid of them
challenge.explanation: Their continued growth shows that the oppression did not weaken them as the Egyptians hoped; they endured and even increased.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “they were grieved because of the children of Israel” reveal about the Egyptians’ feelings?
answers: The Egyptians rejoiced at their success
The Egyptians wanted to join Israel
The Egyptians became troubled and distressed by their presence
challenge.explanation: The phrase expresses distress and uneasiness; the growth of the children of Israel increased the Egyptians’ fear and hostility.

questions.question: What change in the treatment of the children of Israel is described between Joseph’s time and the time of the new king?
answers: The king who knew Joseph was replaced by one who did not know him
Joseph became king instead of Pharaoh
The children of Israel moved from Egypt to another land
questions.explanation: The text emphasizes that the new king “knew not Joseph,” so he did not regard the Israelites with the recognition and appreciation shown earlier.

questions.explanation: Their continued growth shows that the oppression did not weaken them as the Egyptians hoped; they endured and even increased.

answers: The Egyptians rejoiced at their success

The Egyptians became troubled and distressed by their presence
questions.explanation: The phrase expresses distress and uneasiness; the growth of the children of Israel increased the Egyptians’ fear and hostility.

easy.question: Who made the children of Israel work?
answers: The Egyptians
The Midianites
The Philistines
easy.explanation: The verse says, “The Egyptians made the children of Israel to serve.”

easy.question: How did the Egyptians make the lives of the children of Israel bitter?
answers: Through great rest
Through hard labor
Through gifts
easy.explanation: The verse says, “They made their lives bitter with hard bondage.”

easy.question: What materials did the children of Israel work with?
answers: Stone and wood
Gold and silver
Mortar and brick
easy.explanation: The verse specifically mentions mortar and brick.

medium.question: Which description includes both construction work and agricultural work?
answers: In mortar and brick, and in all manner of service in the field
In rest and joy
In war and trade
medium.explanation: The verse mentions mortar and brick as well as “all manner of service in the field.”

medium.question: What does the phrase “with rigour” mean in the context of their labor?
answers: Voluntary work
Harsh and burdensome labor
Short and easy work
medium.explanation: “With rigour” describes harsh, demanding labor, as shown by the reference to hard bondage and bitter lives.

medium.question: What was the result of the hard labor imposed on the children of Israel?
answers: They became wealthy
They moved to another land
Their lives became bitter
medium.explanation: The verse connects the hard bondage with the result: “They made their lives bitter.”

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the repetition of “all manner of service” and “all their service”?
answers: The work imposed on them was broad and comprehensive
They worked for only one day
They chose their own work
challenge.explanation: The repetition emphasizes that they were not assigned just one task, but many kinds of work.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “all manner of service in the field” show about the areas of their labor?
answers: They worked only on building houses
They also performed agricultural work in the fields
They were not required to work outside the cities
challenge.explanation: The phrase adds fieldwork to the work with mortar and brick, showing that their labor included different areas.

challenge.question: Which description combines the manner of their employment, the types of work, and the result?
answers: The Egyptians forced Israel to work harshly at various tasks, and their lives became bitter
Israel worked willingly and received great wages
The Egyptians freed Israel after the brickmaking
challenge.explanation: The two verses describe forced, difficult labor, many kinds of work, and the bitter result of that labor.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the repetition of “all manner of service” and “all their service”?
answers: The work imposed on them was broad and comprehensive

They chose their own work
questions.explanation: The repetition emphasizes that they were not assigned just one task, but many kinds of work.

questions.explanation: The phrase adds fieldwork to the work with mortar and brick, showing that their labor included different areas.

questions.explanation: The two verses describe forced, difficult labor, many kinds of work, and the bitter result of that labor.

easy.question: To whom did the king of Egypt speak?
answers: The Hebrew midwives
The elders of Israel
The army commanders
easy.explanation: Verse 15 says that the king of Egypt spoke to the Hebrew midwives.

easy.question: What were the names of the midwives?
answers: Miriam and Ephrath
Shiphrah and Puah
Rachel and Leah
easy.explanation: The verse names the midwives Shiphrah and Puah.

easy.question: What did the king of Egypt command them to do when a Hebrew son was born?
answers: Raise him in the palace
Hide him
Kill him
easy.explanation: The king of Egypt commanded them to kill every Hebrew son who was born.

medium.question: Why did the midwives not do what the king of Egypt commanded?
answers: Because they feared God
Because they feared the people
Because they did not hear the command
medium.explanation: The verse explains that the midwives feared God, so they did not obey the king’s command.

medium.question: What does the phrase “upon the stools” mean in the context of childbirth?
answers: On musical instruments
On the birthing seats
On building stones
medium.explanation: The context concerns Hebrew women giving birth, so “upon the stools” refers to the seats used during childbirth.

medium.question: What did the midwives do after hearing the king’s command?
answers: They killed only the sons
They left Egypt
They kept the children alive and did not kill them
medium.explanation: Despite the command to kill the sons, the midwives preserved the children’s lives.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the fact that the midwives obeyed God’s will rather than the king’s will?
answers: They regarded obedience to God as their highest duty
They wanted to become queens
They did not understand the king’s words
challenge.explanation: The verse emphasizes their fear of God, so they chose not to harm the children.

challenge.question: What central contrast appears between the king of Egypt’s command and the midwives’ action?
answers: The king wanted the daughters hidden, and they revealed them
The king wanted the sons killed, and they kept the children alive
The king wanted the sons saved, and they killed them
challenge.explanation: The king commanded that a son be killed, while the midwives disobeyed and preserved the children.

challenge.question: Why is it important that the verse explicitly names the midwives?
answers: To show that they were queens of Egypt
To state how many children they saved
To emphasize that they were identifiable individuals who acted courageously
challenge.explanation: Naming them presents the midwives as distinct figures and highlights their courage in opposing the king’s command.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the fact that the midwives obeyed God’s will rather than the king’s will?
answers: They regarded obedience to God as their highest duty
They wanted to become queens
They did not understand the king’s words
questions.explanation: The verse emphasizes their fear of God, so they chose not to harm the children.

easy.question: Who called the midwives and asked why they had kept the children alive?
answers: The king of Egypt
God
The Hebrew women
easy.explanation: Verse 18 says that the king of Egypt called the midwives and questioned them about their actions.

easy.question: What did the midwives do for the babies?
answers: They hid them in Egypt
They kept them alive
They handed them over to Pharaoh
easy.explanation: The verse says, “They saved the men children alive.”

easy.question: What happened to the people after God dealt well with the midwives?
answers: The people left Egypt
The people became weaker
The people multiplied and became very mighty
easy.explanation: Verse 20 says, “The people multiplied, and waxed very mighty.”

medium.question: Why did Pharaoh ask the midwives why they had kept the children alive?
answers: Because he expected them to kill the children
Because he wanted to praise them
Because he did not know who they were
medium.explanation: Pharaoh expected the midwives to obey his command, so he asked why they had left the children alive.

medium.question: What does the phrase “they are lively” mean in this context?
answers: The women are vigorous and give birth quickly
The women are wild animals
The women are unable to give birth
medium.explanation: The context says that the women gave birth before the midwife arrived, so “lively” describes them as vigorous and quick to deliver.

medium.question: What is the correct order of events in these verses?
answers: God made houses for the midwives, and then they feared him
The people became strong, and then Pharaoh called the midwives
The midwives feared God, God dealt well with them, and the people multiplied
medium.explanation: First the midwives feared God; afterward God dealt well with them, and the people multiplied and became strong.

challenge.question: What explanation did the midwives give for not killing the children?
answers: The children hid from them
The Hebrew women gave birth before the midwife arrived
Pharaoh had canceled his command
challenge.explanation: The midwives said that the Hebrew women gave birth quickly, before they arrived, so they could not carry out Pharaoh’s command.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the connection between the midwives’ actions and the growth of the people?
answers: Their actions helped ensure that the people continued to grow rather than decrease
Their actions caused the people to leave Egypt
Their actions caused Pharaoh to stop ruling
challenge.explanation: Despite Pharaoh’s command, the midwives kept the children alive, and the verse emphasizes that the people multiplied and became very mighty.

challenge.question: What does the verse present as the reason God made “houses” for the midwives?
answers: They were Egyptian midwives
They feared God
They asked Pharaoh for payment
challenge.explanation: The verse directly connects the midwives’ fear of God with God’s making houses for them.

questions.question: What explanation did the midwives give for not killing the children?
answers: The children hid from them
The Hebrew women gave birth before the midwife arrived
Pharaoh had canceled his command
questions.explanation: The midwives said that the Hebrew women gave birth quickly, before they arrived, so they could not carry out Pharaoh’s command.

questions.explanation: Despite Pharaoh’s command, the midwives kept the children alive, and the verse emphasizes that the people multiplied and became very mighty.

answers: They were Egyptian midwives

They asked Pharaoh for payment
questions.explanation: The verse directly connects the midwives’ fear of God with God’s making houses for them.

paragraphs.title: The Decree to Throw the Sons into the River

easy.question: To whom did Pharaoh command his decree to be carried out?
answers: All his people
Only his soldiers
Only the midwives
easy.explanation: The verse explicitly says that Pharaoh charged all his people.

easy.question: What did Pharaoh command should be done to every son who was born?
answers: Raise him in the palace
Cast him into the river
Send him into the wilderness
easy.explanation: Pharaoh commanded, “Every son that is born ye shall cast into the river.”

easy.question: What did Pharaoh command should be done to every daughter who was born?
answers: Cast her into the river
Sell her
Save her alive
easy.explanation: The end of the verse says, “Every daughter ye shall save alive.”

medium.question: How did Pharaoh’s decree for the sons differ from his decree for the daughters?
answers: The sons were to be cast into the river, and the daughters were to be kept alive
The sons were to be kept alive, and the daughters were to be cast into the river
Both sons and daughters were to be sent into the wilderness
medium.explanation: The verse gives different instructions according to the child’s sex: sons were to be cast into the river, while daughters were to be kept alive.

medium.question: What does the phrase “save alive” mean in this context?
answers: Teach her
Keep her alive
Cast her away
medium.explanation: “Save alive” means to preserve her life; the contrast with casting the sons into the river makes this clear.

medium.question: Why can it be said that the command was aimed especially at harming the future survival of Israel?
answers: Because it forbade everyone to work
Because it commanded all the women to be expelled
Because it specifically targeted newborn boys
medium.explanation: The command targeted every newborn son, thereby attacking the male generation and the future continuation of the people.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the fact that the command was given to “all his people”?
answers: The decree was a public and widespread order
The decree concerned only Pharaoh’s family
The decree was a private suggestion to the midwives
challenge.explanation: The phrase “all his people” shows that Pharaoh wanted the entire population to take part in carrying out the decree.

challenge.question: Which detail emphasizes that the command applied to every son who was born?
answers: The word “daughter”
The word “every”
The word “river”
challenge.explanation: The word “every” emphasizes that the command applied to all newborn sons without exception.

challenge.question: What is the central contrast in the structure of the verse?
answers: Between Pharaoh and his people
Between Egypt and the wilderness
Between the fate of the sons and the fate of the daughters
challenge.explanation: The verse sets the command to cast the sons into the river against the command to save the daughters alive.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the fact that the command was given to “all his people”?
answers: The decree was a public and widespread order
The decree concerned only Pharaoh’s family
The decree was a private suggestion to the midwives
questions.explanation: The phrase “all his people” shows that Pharaoh wanted the entire population to take part in carrying out the decree.

answers: Between Pharaoh and his people
